extraction.name: EgoLife Dataset
extraction.description: EgoLife is a project to develop an egocentric life assistant that accompanies and enhances personal efficiency through AI-powered wearable glasses. To lay the foundation for this assistant, a comprehensive data collection study was conducted where six participants lived together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities—including discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment—using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references. This effort resulted in the EgoLife Dataset, a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.citeAs: The EgoLife Team. EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.03803, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The EgoLife dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment, called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded the participants’ activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized, comprehensive multimodal analysis of daily events and interactions. During the week, participants were asked to organize an Earth Day party on the second-to-last day, involving meetings, discussions, rehearsals, cooking, and house decoration. Activities extended beyond the house, including shopping and sightseeing, with recording permission obtained. Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations, with glasses collected every three hours for data upload and storage clearance (approximately one hour). During this period, participants were instructed to remain in their rooms and limit activities to resting or non-essential tasks to prevent logic disruptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Six participants wore Meta Aria glasses, recording approximately 8 hours of egocentric video and signals daily. 15 GoPro cameras and 2 mmWave devices provided synchronized third-person perspective data. For the Milan dataset, 6 indoor third-person cameras, 2 TI IWR6843 (60GHz) mmWave monostatic radars, one AWR1843 (77GHz) mmWave monostatic radar, and 3 Asus RT-AX82U WiFi receivers/emitters were used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day period (Beijing dataset), one-day session (Milan dataset)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rigorous data cleaning process was implemented to ensure synchronization, participant privacy, and readiness for annotation and data release. This included: Multimodal Signal Extraction (radar and WiFi extracted and aligned with video), Multi-view Synchronization (video and signal data synchronized using timestamps), De-identification Process (all identifiable faces and sensitive license plates blurred, sensitive audio topics muted), and Audio Processing (audio processed to mute sensitive information and enhance clarity for Q&A annotations).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations were created by merging audio tracks from six participants, applying speech recognition [90] to generate initial timestamped transcripts, and then using a diarization algorithm [91] to differentiate speakers. This 50-hour transcript was reviewed for accuracy, then split into six tracks, refined by reviewers to keep only speech audible to each participant. Caption annotations involved splitting videos into 5-minute clips, slowed to 0.8x speed, for annotators to provide continuous narrations covering actions, interactions, and environmental details. Narrations were converted to text via transcription, reviewed, and corrected. Initial narrations (361K phrases) were merged into 25K 'merged captions' using GPT-4o-mini, then expanded into 'visual-audio captions' by pairing with representative frames and transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o, and verified by human annotators. EgoLifeQA annotations involved designing five question types (EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster). Prompts were crafted for each type and fed 'visual-audio captions' into GPT-4o in batches, generating around 100K timestamped questions per participant. These AI-generated questions served as a filtering and inspiration tool for annotators, who retained only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior, with a preference for longer dependencies and real-world relevance. After selection and refinement, 500 high-quality QAs per participant were curated. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions, annotated audio requirements, and specified look-back time.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Capcut (video editing software with dubbing functions [92]), GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The 50-hour transcript was reviewed for accuracy. Reviewers refined each audio track, keeping only the speech audible to each participant. Narrations were converted to text via a transcription tool, then reviewed and corrected for a synchronized, time-aligned textual description. Visual-audio captions were verified by human annotators. AI-generated questions for EgoLifeQA acted as a filtering and inspiration tool for annotators, helping them identify valuable instances. Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with a preference for those demanding longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance. This streamlined process enabled the efficient creation of a high-quality QA dataset tailored to long-context reasoning and practical real-world tasks. A final round of meticulous revision resulted in a carefully crafted set of 500 QA per participant.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 361K brief, subtitle-like phrases (narrations), 25K merged captions, 500 QA per participant (for EgoLifeQA)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper Large v3 (speech recognition [90]), diarization algorithm [91], GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: This is an ongoing project that aims to document human daily activities in natural environments. The plan is to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities, and to develop more sophisticated models. The partnership with the annotation team will continue for future EgoLife versions.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Faces (participants and bystanders), personal identities, private audio conversations, personal data displayed on screens (e.g., passwords, personal data), vehicle license plates.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The EgoLife project has significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction through personalized and context-aware assistance, improving quality of life for individuals needing support (e.g., elderly, those with cognitive challenges). It can facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development in educational and professional settings. However, deep integration into personal spaces necessitates addressing privacy and ethical considerations to ensure user autonomy and trust. Safeguards for data privacy and transparency in AI decision-making processes are crucial for positive societal reception, aiming to foster a new era of AI companions that support individuals in a socially and ethically responsible manner.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was intentionally started with a narrow setting (e.g., single language/scenario for the Beijing dataset), sacrificing some generalizability, which can lead to biases when applied to broader contexts. Models trained on the dataset (EgoGPT) tend to overfit to early observations for personalization, potentially misidentifying individuals if their appearance changes (e.g., misidentifying a different person wearing blue later as the same individual if a person wore a blue shirt on Day-1).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset was intentionally started with a narrow setting (e.g., single language/scenario for the Beijing dataset), which limits its generalizability. Models trained on this dataset have limitations: EgoGPT’s speech understanding remains incomplete, struggling to understand human laughter and emotions, likely due to its reliance on ASR-trained data. Identity recognition is a challenge, with the model tending to overfit to early observations, potentially leading to misidentification. EgoRAG’s retrieval mechanism lacks multi-step reasoning, performing a single-pass search without iterative refinement, making it prone to failure when relevant information is missing from direct retrieval and lacking error tolerance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Development of state-of-the-art multimodal egocentric AI assistants, advancing long-term egocentric life assistance, training and fine-tuning models (e.g., EgoGPT), generating QA candidates, and serving as a benchmark for long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks (EgoLifeQA). Usage guidelines include addressing practical questions such as recalling past relevant events, monitoring health habits, and offering personalized recommendations.
